environment.path: Physical Wi-Fi LAN; direct UDP; one PeerConnection / SCTP association / ordered DataChannel; empty recvonly video on every arm

scope.input: Production sealed records prepared from cached synthetic input before timing.
scope.output: Browser memory; ciphertext hash plus full plaintext authentication/integrity for complete transfers.
scope.timing: Browser request until complete plaintext authentication; first-byte excludes ICE/DTLS setup and input preparation.
scope.interactive: 16-byte request echoed through the same ordered FrameChannel every 200 ms; measures transport contention, not the full preview UI.
scope.cancellation: Connection shutdown requested 500 ms after streaming starts; does not represent cancellation of one content operation while preserving other work.
scope.ordinaryBatch: Ready SCTP/DTLS batches amortize locking/context setup; ordinary Windows UDP writes are still sequential.
scope.overlappedBatch: At most the configured ready batch is submitted using raw WSASendTo before waiting; Go ordinary UDP already uses overlapped I/O.
scope.compact: Removes the pion/transport replacement through netctx.PacketConn.Conn(); preserves the earlier experimental deadline adapter for comparison.
scope.statistics: Three repeats per large/interactivity/cancel/compact arm; four per small-file arm; alternate order. Throughput and duration medians use the mean of the middle pair for even counts. Echo percentiles are pooled samples selected by ceil((n-1)*q), not independent trials.
limits: Wi-Fi varied; before/after TCP controls moved substantially. Absolute rates and three-run differences do not establish universal gains.
The new native completion lifecycle is a design; the throughput prototype still has a fixed two-second cancellation fallback.
No final production implementation, disk-backed sender/receiver, full UI preview path, or physical WAN performance was measured.
This round measures Windows sender to Linux browser only. Earlier Linux-to-Windows gains involved combined changes.
The ownership model uses fixed lane windows and synthetic output settlement; it is not a replacement production scheduler.
Protected preview capacity was modeled by splitting the same total budget, reducing bulk-only retention by one modeled block; its product tuning and throughput trade-off are not measured.
Pending native lifecycle probes use receives to force a stable pending state. Each deadline/close observation is 50 ms; reported sub-tick cancellation times are not a zero-latency guarantee.
Linux UDP counters are host-global and can include unrelated activity. They are not proof of loss on an individual trial.
Compact adapter interop succeeded, but its pooled echo latency was noisier/higher; performance equivalence is not established.
No 40 MB/s sustained physical-path claim is made.

decisions.decision: Preserve ready batches through SCTP, DTLS and ICE, without waiting to fill a batch.
decisions.why: Long-transfer ablation supports reduced per-packet overhead, while small files show no stable gain from native concurrency. Keep first/tail datagrams immediate and one bounded service turn.

decisions.decision: Keep original production buffer watermarks during the transport refactor.
decisions.why: 4 MiB / 90% increased pooled echo p95 from 64 to 329.6 ms for only about 0.7% median throughput gain versus overlap16 at the original watermarks.

decisions.decision: Refactor existing public allocation at the capacity claim boundary.
decisions.why: Actual browser broker/window composition admitted a later preview ninth. A claim-with-reservation model admitted it second. No multi-connection orchestration is needed to obtain this property.

decisions.decision: Keep response capacity, output retention, and cache authorities distinct.
decisions.why: Receiving a fragment replenishes network capacity but does not free memory owned by authentication/output. Collapsing output authorities lets a stalled bulk sink block other consumers.

decisions.decision: Use one native send owner with explicit cancellation and drain.
decisions.why: Nine real pending Windows overlapped receive probes showed Go deadlines or Go-close-first cannot settle a manually owned pending operation; explicit CancelIoEx followed by completion does.

decisions.decision: Remove the additional pion/transport fork from the integration design.
decisions.why: The existing Conn accessor exposes the underlying capability. Six cross-machine transfers with an unmodified netctx module passed full content integrity. The adapter is functional evidence, not a finished lifecycle implementation.

decisions.decision: Contain unavoidable platform complexity and delete superseded coordination.
decisions.why: A native backend adds local complexity. The architectural improvement depends on removing per-lane task queues and duplicate timeout machinery, preserving existing owners, and keeping consumers free of OS details and experimental switches.

reference.meaning: Actual broker/allocator/window composition with a gated lane; deterministic scheduling evidence, not a network latency measurement.

randomized.limitation: A focused ownership model with fixed lane windows; not an implementation or throughput claim.

nativeLifecycle.meaning: Actual Windows overlapped receive operations on private loopback sockets; verifies cancellation/descriptor ownership, not UDP send throughput.

sourceFindings.finding: Claims a lane and removes public work before the lane receive window admits it.
A private asynchronous receive-window wait follows lane assignment.
Fragment-based replenishment and rate estimation already exist; preserve this behavior while removing its private task queue.
Read-ahead currently reserves output capacity for queued descriptors before dispatch.
Allocation chooses queued work and ranked lanes before receive capacity admission.
Native range refill currently follows ordered sink writes; native and browser supply behavior must be examined separately.
Native receiver already owns bounded plaintext reservation and shared-load lifecycle.
Uncertain send errors remain conservatively accepted; local completion is not remote delivery.
Production FrameChannel owns application admission and cancellation disposition.
Production send watermarks remain unchanged.
Existing authority constructs and owns physical sockets and Pion mux resources.
Endpoint write deadlines delegate to a shared underlying connection.
Shared socket deadline cancellation already requires coordinated writer state.
ICE write deadline controls the selected candidate path.

externalSources.supports: Cancellation requests do not release OVERLAPPED/buffer ownership; completion must still be observed, and completion may race cancellation.
Local overlapped completion and datagram submission do not mean remote delivery.
The descriptor remains valid during the Control callback.
Go uses overlapped Windows operations with its own write serialization/cancellation ownership.

reproduction.requirements: Existing local research source copies, installed Go/Node/Playwright, synthetic payload files, and authorized Linux SSH/Chrome host; not a portable clean-checkout benchmark.
reproduction.cleanup: Each cross-machine batch received the isolated remote Chrome/profile cleanup acknowledgement.

reviewFollowup.scope: Current browser production classes with controlled responses, plus Windows loopback native I/O probes. No proposed production scheduler or full-file performance claim.

unavailableRoute.setup: Actual broker and lane set, one ready direct lane; older relay-only work consumes every upstream slot.
Actual broker and lane set, one ready direct lane; older relay-only work consumes every upstream slot.

independentRangeCopies.meaning: One shared authenticated block can produce two independently owned range slices; network singleflight does not deduplicate these copies.

stalledOutput.meaning: Actual range windows exhaust a 2 MiB output budget while a bulk generator is paused; preview priority alone cannot create capacity.

supply.scope: Deterministic probes against current production classes with controlled network responses; no throughput or proposed implementation claim.

partialCompletion.stimulus: A 65,508-byte IPv4 UDP datagram between two valid datagrams. This is fault injection, not a proposed production MTU.
partialCompletion.implication: Windows concurrent-operation completion cannot be summarized as a successful prefix. Preserve individual ownership and do not blindly replay the batch or suffix.

native.cancellation: Targeted cancellation preserved another pending operation on the same socket. Go read deadlines interrupted Go reads but did not settle manually owned overlapped operations. Close waited for both RawConn-protected operations to drain.
native.limits: Receive operations force deterministic pending states; sends exercise real partial completion. These probes do not establish send-cancellation latency or file-operation cancellation behavior.

dependencyAudit.netctx: The unmodified v4.1.0 Conn accessor exposes the underlying PacketConn; direct calls bypass the wrapper write mutex and deadline cancellation. The new send owner must replace those responsibilities explicitly.
dependencyAudit.addressStorage: The initial follow-up send probe copied the experimental RawSockaddrInet4-to-RawSockaddrAny upcast and failed checkptr. The passing probe allocates RawSockaddrAny storage and pins it; the earlier experiment is unchanged.

sourceFindings.finding: Global dispatch slots are consumed before lane capacity/availability; work with no eligible route can therefore occupy a slot while usable work waits.
Range descriptors reserve output bytes before upstream admission, so a preview may be blocked before entering public allocation.
Shared block loads still produce separate range-consumer copies.
Native shared loads also return independently allocated consumer copies.
Protected interactive headroom must accommodate actual block geometry; supported chunk sizes reach 4 MiB.
Native range refill follows ordered sink writes; align ownership without copying browser output semantics.

reproduction.requirements: Retained local research files, installed Node/Go and browser dependencies; Windows for native probes. Not a portable clean-checkout benchmark.

remaining: Protected interactive headroom is necessary for independent progress under a stalled bulk sink; its production size and bulk-throughput cost remain to be measured.
Linux batch submission was source-audited but not executed in this follow-up.
Portable versus native complete-file benefit, full preview latency, disk output, and physical WAN behavior require the implementation and end-to-end runs.
